pointOnly.name: Bonus point only (any drawing you did not apply for that year)
pointOnly.quote: You may purchase one bonus point per license type per year, either at the time of application or between July 1 and Sept. 30 of the current year if you did not apply for that license type.

pointOnly.name: Nonresident combination preference point only
pointOnly.quote: Those who do not apply for a combination license may purchase one preference point for $100 over the counter from July 1 through December 31.

fees.label: Conservation license (resident, 18-61)
fees.quote: Conservation License is a prerequisite for all resident and nonresident licenses ... Resident Cost: $8

fees.label: Conservation license (nonresident)
fees.quote: Conservation License is a prerequisite for all resident and nonresident licenses ... Nonresident Cost: $10

fees.label: Base hunting license fee (resident)
fees.quote: Base hunting license fee ... will be assessed at the time the hunter purchases or applies for his/her first hunting license ... Resident Cost: $10

fees.label: Base hunting license fee (nonresident)
fees.quote: Base hunting license fee ... will be assessed at the time the hunter purchases or applies for his/her first hunting license ... Nonresident Cost: $50

fees.label: Resident general elk license (18-61)
fees.notes: Required before applying for a resident elk permit. Youth and 62+: $10.

fees.label: Resident general deer license (18-61)
fees.notes: Required before applying for a resident deer permit. Youth and 62+: $8.

fees.label: Application fee - most drawings (resident and nonresident)
fees.quote: all applications require a nonrefundable $5 application fee. The exception is moose, sheep, goat and bison

fees.label: Moose, sheep, goat application fee (resident)
fees.quote: There is a $10 resident/$50 nonresident nonrefundable application fee required with the application.

fees.label: Moose, sheep, goat application fee (nonresident)
fees.quote: There is a $10 resident/$50 nonresident nonrefundable application fee required with the application.

fees.label: Bonus point at time of application (resident)
fees.quote: the $20 (nonresident) or $2 (resident) bonus point fee for each license/ permit will be added to the total.

fees.label: Bonus point at time of application (nonresident)
fees.quote: the $20 (nonresident) or $2 (resident) bonus point fee for each license/ permit will be added to the total.

fees.label: Bonus point only, July 1 - Sept. 30 (resident)
fees.quote: The fee to purchase a bonus point without applying is $15 per species for residents

fees.label: Bonus point only, July 1 - Sept. 30 (nonresident; deer, elk, antelope)
fees.quote: the nonresident fees are $25 per species with the exception of moose, sheep, and goat, which are $75 per species.

fees.label: Bonus point only, July 1 - Sept. 30 (nonresident; moose, sheep, goat)

fees.label: Nonresident combination preference point
fees.notes: Outfitter clients may buy a second (outfitter-only) point for another $100; max 3 points.
fees.quote: If you elect to purchase a preference point, select "YES" on the preference point question. The additional $100 fee will be added to your total.

fees.label: Nonresident General Big Game (deer + elk) Combination
fees.notes: Includes season fishing and upland bird licenses; conservation, base hunting and AIS pass bought separately. Refund options (80%/50%) exist; see source.

fees.label: Elk permit - drawing (resident and nonresident cost to apply)
fees.notes: Must be used with a general elk license (resident) or combination/elk license (nonresident).
fees.quote: Elk Permit - Drawing only $9.00 ... April 1 ... Elk permits are nonrefundable.

fees.label: Deer permit - drawing (resident and nonresident cost to apply)
fees.quote: Deer Permit - Drawing only $5.00 April 1 Application fee only.

fees.label: Resident antelope (drawing)
fees.notes: 2026 regs list $19.00 total to apply (license + application fee).

fees.label: Resident moose
fees.notes: Moose, sheep, goat license fees are due only if drawn.

prerequisites.text: Buy a conservation license and pay the base hunting license fee (charged when you first buy or apply each license year).
prerequisites.quote: Montana's Conservation License is a prerequisite for all resident and nonresident licenses.

prerequisites.text: Residents must hold the current-year general elk (or general deer) license to apply for an elk (or deer) permit.
prerequisites.quote: Residents must have current year General Elk License to apply. A permit must be used in conjunction with a General Elk License.

prerequisites.text: Nonresidents must also apply for a deer or elk (combination) license when applying for a deer or elk permit.
prerequisites.quote: Nonresidents must also apply for an Elk License when applying for an Elk Permit.

prerequisites.text: Anyone born after January 1, 1985 must show hunter education to buy or apply for a hunting license (Apprentice Hunter program is an alternative for hunting).
prerequisites.quote: To purchase or apply for a Montana hunting license, any person born after January 1, 1985, must provide proof of having successfully completed a hunter education course

prerequisites.text: Moose, bighorn sheep and mountain goat carry a seven-year waiting period after drawing (does not apply to SuperTags).
prerequisites.quote: Moose, bighorn sheep, and mountain goat seven year waiting period does not apply to SuperTags.

notes: No 2027 application dates are posted yet (checked 2026-11-04); FWP's dates page still shows 2026, so all draws are 2026/last_year. The Commission set hunting regulations for both 2026 and 2027, so 2027 is likely similar, but dates are not confirmed. FWP gives drawing results only as 'Mid-April', 'Mid-May', 'Mid-June', 'Early August', so resultsBy is null. Time zone label differs: the web page says '11:45 pm MST' while the 2026 MSGB booklet says '11:45 p.m. (MDT) on May 1'; recorded as 23:45 America/Denver (local Montana time). Fees are the 2026 schedule (fee pages and 2026 regulations). The 2026 fee summary PDF (license-fees-for-2026_web.pdf) has a scrambled text layer, so it was used only as a cross-check. Not captured: AIS prevention pass amount for hunters (page text unclear: $2 resident / $7.50 nonresident appear in tables but column alignment was unclear), bow and arrow license, nonresident deer/elk permit 'license' component beyond the published $5/$9 cost to apply. Bison and the SuperTag lottery are out of scope.
